newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba says general not freed, had temporary pass.
newsitem.headline: Cuba says general not freed, had temporary pass.

text.p: Patricio de la Guardia, a Cuban general condemned to 30 years in jail in the 1989 "Ochoa" case, has not been freed early and has been returned to jail after being allowed out on a temporary permit, the Foreign Ministry said on Thursday.

De la Guardia was released on March 18, the day his elderly father died. Family sources, who said at the time they believed he had been freed for good, said on Wednesday that he was detained again this week.
They said security forces officials who took him from the family home in Havana on Tuesday told him he was being taken to complete formal release papers.

On Thursday, Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Marianela Ferriol said de la Guardia had not been freed for good. She told a regular weekly news briefing that he had been granted a special temporary pass because of family circumstances and had now been returned to jail.

Ferriol, asked for details, said she was aware de la Guardia, who was sentenced in July 1989, had been the subject of foreign media speculation but she did not know if he would end up serving his entire 30-year term since this was the domain of justice authorities. Her remarks were the first Cuban government comment on the case since de la Guardia was let out of jail last week.

De la Guardia, 58, was convicted of drug trafficking and related offences at a trial of officials from the security forces that shocked the communist-ruled island eight years ago. His twin brother Antonio, an Interior Ministry official, was sentenced to death and was shot in July 1989, along with a senior army general, Arnaldo Ochoa, and two other security forces officers.

Ochoa had headed Cuban forces fighting in Angola's civil war and was a military hero before his disgrace. About 10 other officers from the security forces, including Patricio de la Guardia, were given sentences ranging from 15 to 30 years in jail in the case.
De la Guardia appeared on March 19 at the funeral in Havana of his father, Mario de la Guardia, who had died the previous day at the age of 96. He did not speak to reporters.
Family sources appeared convinced that he had been let out of jail for good, although they said at the time they did not know if any conditions were attached to his release.

Iliana de la Guardia, daughter of Antonio, said from her Paris home last week she believed her uncle's release had come thanks to international pressure and the impending trip to Cuba of Pope John Paul II, set for January 1998.
